source_relation: The gartsize module parameter selects an explicit MiB value; auto selects 512 MiB for RS482, and values below 32 MiB or not powers of two fall back to auto.
lock_or_order: Argument validation completes before mc.gtt_size is published.
failure_contract: Invalid explicit values warn and become the family default rather than reaching RS400 programming.
optimization_effect: Defines the requested aperture input but cannot select the workload optimum.
nonclaim: A source-accepted or default size is not a target allocation, stability, or performance verdict.

source_relation: RS400 accepts 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 MiB and maps each to one RS480_VA_SIZE code before setting RS480_GART_EN.
lock_or_order: Size admission precedes page allocation and hardware programming.
failure_contract: An unrecognized size is forced to 32 MiB by adjust_size or rejected by gart_init and gart_enable.
optimization_effect: Proves the four requested encodings exist without preferring one.
nonclaim: A register encoding does not prove that the aperture is usable under pressure.

source_relation: Linux aligns candidate space before and after VRAM to gtt_size, chooses the larger side, reduces an oversized request to the available side, and publishes an inclusive GTT interval.
lock_or_order: VRAM location and gtt_base_align are established before GTT placement.
failure_contract: A request larger than the chosen address region is reduced and warned; the reduced size is not revalidated as a requested denominator member.
optimization_effect: Determines address-space fit and whether a candidate sits before or after the 128 MiB VRAM interval.
nonclaim: The source formula does not make one Vostro address interval timeless.

source_relation: CPU and GPU page counts equal gtt_size divided by their page sizes; Linux allocates one pointer per CPU page, one u64 shadow per GPU page, and RS400 allocates one four-byte hardware PTE per GPU page.
lock_or_order: Page counts precede all three metadata allocations.
failure_contract: Each allocation failure unwinds its completed ownership prefix.
optimization_effect: Quantifies fixed metadata cost for each aperture before payload pages are committed.
nonclaim: GART metadata bytes are not payload capacity, physical backing, or measured pressure.

source_relation: Linux derives GPU-usable VRAM from the northbridge TOM interval and exposes that fixed carve-out to the VRAM manager.
lock_or_order: Northbridge TOM and aperture discovery precede VRAM manager initialization.
failure_contract: Invalid or constrained aperture state can limit driver-visible VRAM, but Linux does not return firmware-reserved DRAM to the operating system.
optimization_effect: Keeps the 128 MiB physical pool distinct from the GTT virtual aperture.
nonclaim: The source relation does not prove that every boot reserves 128 MiB.

source_relation: vramlimit can reduce real_vram_size after the physical VRAM interval is established, and its module description marks the control as testing-only.
lock_or_order: The limit changes driver accounting after vram_start and vram_end derive from the firmware-visible interval.
failure_contract: Zero or a non-power-of-two value leaves the physical interval unchanged and disables the limit.
optimization_effect: Shows that lowering the driver limit cannot reclaim the firmware carve-out and therefore is not a memory optimization.
nonclaim: A smaller reported VRAM size does not increase system RAM or GTT bandwidth.

source_relation: TTM initializes the VRAM range manager maximum from real_vram_size, sets its active size to visible_vram_size, and initializes the GTT range manager from gtt_size.
lock_or_order: The VRAM maximum and active bound initialize before the stolen BO; the GTT manager initializes afterward and before ordinary BO validation.
failure_contract: Each manager reports allocation failure, but later initialization failures return directly; the bounded source does not prove complete rollback of earlier TTM ownership.
optimization_effect: Defines allocator address capacity for the two domains while preserving the visible-versus-total VRAM distinction.
nonclaim: GTT manager capacity is virtual aperture space, not uniquely available physical DRAM.

source_relation: For a multi-domain request Linux appends VRAM, then GTT, then CPU placement; CPU access constrains VRAM to the visible interval.
lock_or_order: Placement construction precedes each TTM validation attempt.
failure_contract: An empty domain request falls back to system placement.
optimization_effect: Makes requested domains and realized placement separate evidence fields.
nonclaim: Preferred order does not prove final placement, residency duration, or lower latency.

source_relation: The per-IB movement threshold decreases from one quarter of VRAM when empty to a one MiB floor at or above half VRAM usage, and validation stops preferred-domain moves only after prior moves cross the threshold.
lock_or_order: The threshold snapshot precedes BO validation and the moved-byte counter brackets each validation.
failure_contract: A preferred-domain validation failure retries with allowed domains unless interrupted.
optimization_effect: Identifies an existing anti-thrash policy that a workload sweep must observe rather than bypass.
nonclaim: The source threshold comment and formula are not a measured optimum for RS482.

source_relation: The maximum single BO size is the unpinned GTT size because VRAM-to-system migration uses the GTT path, including a BO initially requested in VRAM.
lock_or_order: The ceiling is checked before BO creation and before VRAM-to-GTT retry.
failure_contract: An oversized request returns ENOMEM without allocating a BO.
optimization_effect: Shows that a small GTT can constrain VRAM workloads even when nominal VRAM is free.
nonclaim: A larger single-BO ceiling does not prove that physical backing or contiguous aperture remains available.

source_relation: Linux tracks pinned bytes by VRAM or GTT placement and subtracts the respective counters from GEM_INFO visible VRAM and GTT capacity.
lock_or_order: Pin counters change only after successful placement and unwind on unpin.
failure_contract: Failed placement does not publish a pin count.
optimization_effect: Separates nominal capacity from capacity reserved by non-evictable objects.
nonclaim: Unpinned capacity is not the same as the largest allocatable extent.

source_relation: GEM_INFO reports VRAM, visible VRAM, and unpinned GTT capacities; RADEON_INFO reports current VRAM usage, GTT usage, and cumulative bytes moved.
lock_or_order: Queries sample manager and movement state without submitting work.
failure_contract: A failed ioctl yields no observation and cannot be replaced by a zero value.
optimization_effect: Provides the minimum counter set for allocation-pressure and movement comparisons.
nonclaim: Counters alone do not identify fragmentation, cache maintenance, or end-to-end performance.

source_relation: Linux exposes TTM range-manager state as radeon_vram_mm and radeon_gtt_mm and lists every tracked BO size and realized VRAM, GTT, or CPU placement as radeon_gem_info.
lock_or_order: Debugfs registration follows manager and GEM initialization; the GEM list is read under gem.mutex.
failure_contract: Missing debugfs or permission denies the observation and must not be treated as an empty allocator.
optimization_effect: Provides extent and placement evidence needed to distinguish capacity exhaustion from fragmentation.
nonclaim: A debugfs snapshot does not prove stability across a concurrent allocator change or payload correctness.

source_relation: Linux source defines mechanisms and safe counters but cannot choose the optimal GTT aperture for the target.
lock_or_order: A current-configuration no-submit pressure sweep precedes reboot-gated aperture comparisons; submit workloads run only after exact identity and recovery gates.
failure_contract: No candidate closes without retained allocation success, largest extent, placement, movement, workload, stability, and confounder evidence.
optimization_effect: Ranks 128, 256, 512, and 1024 MiB by measured headroom, fragmentation, movement, copy count, stability, and workload outcome.
nonclaim: The largest aperture, highest fill ratio, or lowest metadata cost is not automatically optimal.
